    {
      "title": "Every New Restaurant We Liked In 2024",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/all-the-new-spots-we-liked-in-2024",
      "position": 34,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "[Lucia Pizza’s](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/lucia-pizza-of-soho) tiny sit-down alimentari, directly behind their Soho slice shop, is a pizza party for people who are old enough to occasionally pull their groins. Besides favorites like the creamed spinach slice—all in personal pizza form—there’s good wine, and sides like caesar salad or whipped ricotta with orange blossom honey. Plus tiramisu."
    },
    {
      "title": "Super Cute, Reasonably Priced Restaurants To Catch Up With A Few Friends",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/a-guide-to-the-super-cute-reasonably-priced-restaurant-to-catch-up-with-a-few-friends",
      "position": 26,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Soho’s best-kept secret is Lucia Alimentari, a cafe by day and a sit-down pizza spot by night. Behind [Lucia Pizza](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/lucia-pizza-of-soho), it’s tiny, but usually pretty easy to walk into. They serve all of the slice shop's most beloved pies, like vodka or creamed spinach, just in smaller form. Round out your order with a light and bright caesar salad and some natural wine."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Restaurants In Soho",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/soho-restaurants",
      "position": 4,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "If you spend time in Soho, you might already know about [Lucia Pizza's excellent vodka sauce and creamed spinach slices](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/lucia-pizza-of-soho). But behind its Canal Street location is Lucia Alimentari, a cafe-by-day, wine-bar-by-night from the same team. In the afternoon, stop by for a latte, a focaccia sandwich, and a jar of fancy Italian tomatoes. In the evenings, things get even better. They slide personal-sized pies from the slice shop kitchen through a window into the candlelit alimentari and keep bottles of wine cool in ice-filled tomato tins. Come for a pizza party, and round out your order with a caesar salad and some cold ricotta with orange blossom honey."
    },
    {
      "title": "Where To Have An Affordable Date Night That Still Feels Romantic",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/affordable-dinner-date-ideas",
      "position": 8,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Tucked behind [Lucia Pizza of Soho](https://www.luciapizzaofsoho.com/)—one of the city's [top slice shops](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-pizza-nyc)—is Lucia Alimentari, a tiny sit-down spot where they make personal pies (ranging from $18 to $25) and pour natural wine by candlelight. Everything is made in the slice shop, then slid through a window. Get a creamed spinach and/or vodka pie, one of the rotating small plates and desserts, and lots of Italian wine. Now that you’re in on the secret, go share it with someone. And book a little in advance if you want a primetime reservation."
    }
  ]
}

  "guide_appearances": [
    {
      "title": "19 Unique Outdoor Dining Options In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/14-unique-outdoor-dining-options-in-nyc",
      "position": 12,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Friday through Sunday from 5-10pm, this Greenpoint spot is offering a $70 per person prix-fixe menu of Vietnamese BBQ dishes - like giant prawns and sliced sirloin with lemongrass - which are grilled for you tableside. Reservations for this three-course dinner are required, and can be made through their [website](https://www.diandi.nyc/)."
    },
    {
      "title": "3 Super Bowl Specials To Order Even If You Probably Won’t Turn On The Game",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/3-super-bowl-specials-to-order-even-if-you-probably-wont-turn-on-the-game",
      "position": 1,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "We hate saying “the big game.” It sounds weirdly perverted, or like we’re tiptoeing around using a curse word in front of a six-year-old. What we love, however, is a Buffalo wing dipped in ranch (not its abominable brother, blue cheese). This year, as you exclusively tune into Amanda Gorman’s poetry reading during halftime, make a plan to eat Di An Di’s Vietnamese meat feast that comes with everything from wings, baby back ribs, pork and shrimp rolls, and a hot dog with spicy relish and pickled tomatoes. It costs $35 per person, and you have to place your order by Friday, February 5th."
    },
    {
      "title": "New York City’s Best New Restaurants Of 2018",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-new-restaurants-2018-nyc",
      "position": 2,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "As you might already know, we go to a lot of restaurants. A lot of different restaurants. If we’re doing our jobs well, we should be at a different spot every night of the week. But Di An Di is the new restaurant that’s made us less good at our jobs - because we just want to keep coming back. We find ourselves thinking about the incredible dishes like brisket pho, banh xeo-wrapped summer rolls, and sizzling turmeric catfish when we’re already busy eating other things, and we suggest the plant-covered space for just about every dinner planning situation. We’ve lost count of the number of times we’ve been to this restaurant, but we can tell you that every one of those experiences has been truly excellent."
    },
    {
      "title": "Places That Feel Like You’re Outside When You Really Don’t Want To Leave The A/C",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/airconditioned-places-that-feel-like-youre-outside",
      "position": 7,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Aside from potentially waiting outside on their stoop until your table is ready, the Di An Di experience is a completely indoor one. But the space looks a little more like a plant boutique than most other restaurants, and there’s a nice skylight in the back dining room. This Vietnamese spot makes some of our favorite food in Greenpoint, including an excellent rice paper salad and beef pho hanoi. Do you really want to eat pho on a concrete sidewalk in 90-degree weather? Neither do we."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Noodle Soups In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-noodle-soup-nyc",
      "position": 10,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Beef Phở\n\nYou will feel like an extremely lucky person to be eating any of the five bowls of phở at Đi Ăn Đi. But the beef phở at this Greenpoint spot is the one that keeps us coming back. It’s packed with tender brisket, noodles, an egg yolk, and handfuls of scallions, and could be shared with a group. We recommend you hoard as much of it for yourself as you can."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Outdoor Date Night Spots In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-date-night-nyc-outdoor",
      "position": 10,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Any night that ends with you drinking pho broth straight from the bowl at Di An Di should be considered a success. But if you want a bit more pomp and circumstance, make a reservation for a table on the weekend, when this Greenpoint spot offers a prix-fixe menu of Vietnamese BBQ dishes that are grilled tableside."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Restaurants In Greenpoint",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-greenpoint-restaurants",
      "position": 11,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "If you're reading this and you still haven’t been to Đi Ăn Đi, we hope you’re having a nice day, and we also hope you stop reading this and go to Đi Ăn Đi. Ideally, you'll bring a few friends to this Vietnamese restaurant and tackle as much of the menu as you can. But if you don't have anyone who currently wants to eat with you, a bowl of the brisket phở at the bar is an excellent solo dining choice."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Vietnamese Restaurants In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/the-best-vietnamese-restaurants-in-nyc",
      "position": 6,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Ordering nothing but phở at this breezy Greenpoint spot is like only listening to pre-psychedelics Beatles. You’ll be happy, but oblivious to the fact that it can get even better. That’s why alongside your beef phở with wok-seared brisket, or the lighter version with poached chicken, your order should include a few more things, like crunchy chả giò packed with pork and shrimp. This pastel-colored restaurant has been packed since it opened in 2018, and while you could come here for a cocktail and soup by yourself at the bar, the best way to experience Đi Ăn Đi is with a few people and a large appetite."
    },
    {
      "title": "Where To Eat Outside In Greenpoint",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/where-to-eat-outside-in-greenpoint-nyc",
      "position": 2,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Friday through Sunday, this Greenpoint spot is offering a $70 three-course prix-fixe menu of Vietnamese BBQ dishes, like grilled rice paper with clams and sliced sirloin with lemongrass. The three seatings per night for parties of two can be reserved through their [website](https://www.diandi.nyc/), or if you’d rather order from their a la carte takeout menu, you can do so any day except Monday, and eat at seat-yourself tables out front Tuesday through Thursday."
    },
    {
      "title": "Where To Eat Outside When It’s Cold & Rainy In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/nyc-rain-restaurants-outdoor-dining",
      "position": 7,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Like a rain shower, a gust of cold subway wind, or a friend who tends to be too honest, the Vietnamese food at Di An Di is refreshing and necessary every few months. This Greenpoint restaurant’s noodle soups are perfect for cold nights."
    },
    {
      "title": "Where To Eat Seriously Good Phở In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/where-to-eat-pho-in-nyc",
      "position": 9,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "You’ll feel like an extremely lucky person to be eating any of the five bowls of phở alongside a nice glass of wine at Đi Ăn Đi in Greenpoint. But the phở thìn hà nội is the one that keeps us coming back. It’s packed with tender brisket, noodles, and at least two large handfuls of scallions, along with an egg yolk on top—and it could easily be shared amongst four people. We recommend you hoard as much of it for yourself as you can."
    },
    {
      "title": "Where To Go When Someone Hates Cheese",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/where-to-go-when-someone-hates-cheese",
      "position": 19,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "One of our [favorite new restaurants of 2018](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-new-restaurants-2018-nyc) is also an excellent place to continue pursuing your cheese-free lifestyle. In part because you can come here and eat “pizza” that has no cheese of any kind (it’s made of rice paper and topped with things like egg and pork, or mung bean spread and vegetables). You’ll want the pho with fatty brisket, too, and the fried daikon rice cake omelette."
    }
  ]
}

  "review": {
    "title": "Cocina Consuelo",
    "headline": "Cocina Consuelo is a New York love song",
    "summary": "A dream-come-true dinner party, with excellent Mexican food.",
    "author": "Sonal Shah",
    "published_at": "2026-01-26T15:00:00.000Z",
    "url": "https://theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/cocina-consuelo"
  },
  "tags": {
    "cuisine": [
      "Mexican"
    ],
    "neighborhood": [
      "West Harlem"
    ],
    "occasion": [
      "Date Nights"
    ]
  },
  "guide_appearances": [
    {
      "title": "18 Restaurants That Remind Us Why We Love New York",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/restaurants-that-remind-us-why-we-love-new-york",
      "position": 4,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Happy coincidences abound in NYC. Maybe you found a loaded subway card or ran into that now-single ex-coworker. But if life has been feeling a little less serendipitous lately, head to Cocina Consuelo. The Hamilton Heights restaurant grew out of a Dominican and Mexican couple’s pandemic supper club, and it feels DIY in the best of ways. (You might even leave with a recommendation for a great local daycare or hear a performance from a jazz saxophonist who used to jam with Duke Ellington.) But the difference between Cocina Consuelo and a regular old apartment party is that the food and drinks—pineapple espresso and fluffy masa pancakes for brunch, birria-topped bone marrow and Mexican wine at dinner—are far more serious."
    },
    {
      "title": "9 Great Birria Tacos In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/great-birria-tacos-nyc",
      "position": 8,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "This is technically cheating, but Cocina Consuelo did begin life as a birria taco pop-up, so we’re giving an honorable mention to the birria bone marrow dish at this small, brightly colored Hamilton Heights restaurant. The couple who runs the place simmer their birria for over 15 hours, and serve it at dinner time, spooned over halved marrow bones and topped with pickled onions, cilantro, and salsa roja. There’s a delicious mix of meat and fatty marrow in each bite, which you scoop up with earthy sweet, fresh tortillas."
    },
    {
      "title": "Every New Restaurant We Liked In 2024",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/all-the-new-spots-we-liked-in-2024",
      "position": 75,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "It feels like anything could happen at this tiny uptown restaurant, which grew out of a couple's pandemic supper club. At dinner, someone may feel so moved by their birria bone marrow that they jump up and start playing the warbly piano. At brunch, a baby might be handed around the room as its mother focuses on her corn pudding-like masa pancake. The Mexican food is excellent, and the sense of possibility strong."
    },
    {
      "title": "NYC Restaurants Offering Valentine’s Day Specials",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/nyc-valentines-day-specials",
      "position": 3,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "This Harlem restaurant doesn't normally take reservations, but they're making an exception for Valentine's Day this year. There will be [two seatings](https://www.instagram.com/p/DUEivsVklgd/?hl=en), with three course meals, a glass of wine, and live music. Text to reserve (347-552-4193)."
    },
    {
      "title": "NYC’s Best New Restaurants Of 2024",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-new-restaurants-new-york-2024",
      "position": 5,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "#### THE MOMENT WE KNEW WE LOVED IT\n\nWhen our fork cut a fluffy, satisfying swath through the fruit-topped masa pancake.\n\n#### A PERFECT ORDER FOR WEEKDAY BRUNCH\n\nFried tortilla con huevo, a crisp ensalada “César,” and a masa pancake. On Wednesdays, add the kalacreme, a dulce de leche donut.\n\n#### GO IF YOU LIKE…\n\nLittle restaurants with big personalities."
    },
    {
      "title": "The 25 Best New Dishes Of 2024",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-new-dishes-nyc-2024",
      "position": 10,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Masa Pancake\n\nWhen you visit our only uptown [Best New Restaurant](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-new-restaurants-new-york-2024) (and the only one with a piano), go at breakfast and order this. It’s a large, deep brown pancake, sitting in a pool of honey butter, topped with ready-to-burst blueberries. All this would be enough, even without the corn pudding-like texture, the fact that it’s gluten-free, and the cinnamon-spiced café de olla you should drink alongside."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Breakfast In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-breakfast-nyc",
      "position": 5,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "This Mexican spot in Hamilton Heights grew out of a couple’s dinner party series, and there’s a magical quality to the bright yellow little with a big window, a piano, and a tiny kitchen behind the counter. The food is magical too: get at least one order of tortilla con huevo—the fresh tortillas are fried to a light crisp and topped with hoja santa and salsa roja—and one fat, fluffy, honey butter-drenched masa pancake with homemade compote for the table."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Mexican Restaurants In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-mexican-restaurants-nyc",
      "position": 3,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Painted an unmissable, electric Frida Kahlo-blue, this little restaurant in Hamilton Heights grew out of a pandemic supper club run by couple Karina Garcia and Lalo Rodriguez. At night, it still feels like a dinner party, with spontaneous music from an upright piano, laughter, and the smells of great food cooking. Stop by with a date for an evening of fresh, earthy-sweet tortillas to go with your savory, birria-topped bone marrow, or a glass of Mexican wine with a juicy cornish hen stuffed with grains and quelites. We love breakfast here even more, when you can pair some eggs and fried tortillas with a refreshing café de olla or pineapple espresso."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best NYC Restaurants For Dining Solo",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/great-restaurants-for-dining-solo",
      "position": 5,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Eating alone is a far from lonely experience at this Hamilton Heights restaurant, where tight quarters and friendly staff make it easy to strike up a conversation. While you’re sitting at the small, tiled counter, or at a table that’s pushed against a piano, you’ll inevitably swap local recommendations for hairdressers and babysitters over Mexican wine or a cocktail with a flower in it. On Fridays, someone might even be playing that piano while you eat things like birria-topped bone marrow with fresh tortillas, or beets with a blackened outer crust that cracks apart into a tangy chile dressing, fresh requesón with cream, and crunchy pistachios."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Pancakes In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/the-best-pancakes-in-nyc",
      "position": 3,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Everything on the [breakfast](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-breakfast-nyc) menu at this bright yellow-and-blue Mexican restaurant in Hamilton Heights is great, but the masa pancake is the dish you’ll keep flashing back to all day. Get one for the table—it’s fluffier than a freshly dried towel, with gently crisped edges. The huge pancake is drenched through with not-too-sweet honey butter and topped with homemade seasonal fruit compote. It pairs well with a chilled café de olla (sweetened with piloncillo) or an iced pineapple espresso. These are also available at their Upper West Side location, [Consuelo](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/cocina-consuelo-upper-west-side), where you can get them with a side of bacon."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Restaurants In West Harlem & Hamilton Heights",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-restaurants-west-harlem-hamilton-heights",
      "position": 1,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "This little walk-in-only restaurant at 143rd grew out of a pandemic supper club run by couple Karina Garcia and Lalo Rodriguez. At night, their mostly Mexican meals still feel like dinner parties. Someone might spontaneously decide to play an upright piano after more than a few glasses of wine from Baja California. People sit at a handful of tables or at the bar, swiping earthy-sweet tortillas through the last bits of birria and marrow on the halved bones in front of them. As great as dinner is though, we love breakfast even more, when you can pair some eggs and fried tortillas with a refreshing café de olla or pineapple espresso. Get a fluffy, fruit-topped [masa pancake](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/the-best-pancakes-in-nyc) for the table."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Things We Ate In April 2025",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-dishes-we-ate-april-2025",
      "position": 7,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Betabeles\n\nThese chioggia beets are peeled and air-dried before being oven-roasted with a little oil, salt and pepper. Sounds simple enough, but somehow this dish tastes different from all other beet salads, thanks to a blackened outer crust that cracks apart into a tangy chile dressing, fresh requesón with cream, and crunchy pistachios."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Walk-In-Only Restaurants For When You Didn’t Make A Reservation",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/walk-in-only-restaurants",
      "position": 1,
